title: Nakanishi2015 – SSVEP Nakanishi 2015 dataset
description: A 12-class steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) derivative dataset acquired from 9 healthy subjects using 8-channel EEG recorded at 256 Hz with joint frequency-phase modulation. This preprocessed dataset was derived from the original Nakanishi et al. 2015 study and contains bandpass-filtered (6-80 Hz) and downsampled data with a 135-ms latency delay applied to account for visual system delay. The dataset was used to benchmark canonical correlation analysis (CCA)-based methods for SSVEP detection in brain-computer interface applications, demonstrating that individual calibration data significantly improves classification performance compared to standard CCA approaches.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a Biosemi ActiveTwo amplifier with 8 electrodes (PO7, PO3, POz, PO4, PO8, O1, Oz, O2) in standard 10-20 montage at 256 Hz sampling rate from 9 healthy subjects. Subjects performed a 12-class SSVEP target identification task with visual stimuli flickering at frequencies ranging from 9.25 to 14.75 Hz (0.5 Hz resolution). Each trial lasted 4 seconds with a 1-second cue period. Data were preprocessed with zero-phase IIR bandpass filtering (6-80 Hz) and downsampling, with a 135-ms latency delay applied to account for visual system delay. This derivative dataset contains the preprocessed data from the original study.
